title: flash_ctrl: where transmission integrity errors are recorded
conditions: After a transmission integrity error: in program data written by software (R1, R2), in data read by the life cycle management interface (R3), or in program data written by that interface (R4).
Each setting is encoded as 1 if the statement about the design holds and 0 if it does not.

requirements.text: If the data integrity is incorrect, an in-band error response is returned to the initiating host and an error is registered in [`ERR_CODE.PROG_INTG_ERR`](registers.md#err_code).
requirements.note: Section "Host / Software Initiated Access to Flash Macro", about program operations.

requirements.text: An error is also registered in [`STD_FAULT_STATUS.PROG_INTG_ERR`](registers.md#std_fault_status) to indicate that a fatal fault has occurred.
If an integrity error is seen, it is registered in [`FAULT_STATUS.LCMGR_INTG_ERR`](registers.md#fault_status).
requirements.note: Section "Life Cycle Management Interface / Hardware Initiated Access to Flash Macro", about read operations.

requirements.text: If an integrity error is seen, an error is registered in [`FAULT_STATUS.PROG_INTG_ERR`](registers.md#fault_status).

design.text: This could be a program integrity error, see !!STD_FAULT_STATUS.
design.note: ERR_CODE.prog_err (bit 3): "Flash program has an error. This could be a program integrity error".
The program controller reports a program integrity error as its prog_err.

For an operation software started, the arbiter passes the controller's errors to sw_err_o (for a hardware-initiated one, to hw_err_o at line 212); for a program operation the errors come from the program controller (line 247).

design.description: no field of ERR_CODE has "intg" in its name (its fields are op_err, mp_err, rd_err, prog_err, prog_win_err, prog_type_err, update_err and macro_err)

design.note: STD_FAULT_STATUS.prog_intg_err (bit 1): "The flash controller encountered a program data transmission integrity error."
Set by the physical controller's program integrity check, whoever started the operation.

design.description: no field of FAULT_STATUS has "intg" in its name (its fields are op_err, mp_err, rd_err, prog_err, prog_win_err, prog_type_err, seed_err, phy_relbl_err, phy_storage_err, spurious_ack, arb_err and host_gnt_err)

design.note: STD_FAULT_STATUS.lcmgr_intg_err (bit 3): "an integrity error on the generated integrity during a life cycle management interface read".
The interface's integrity error (flash_ctrl_lcmgr.sv line 918) reaches only this field: lcmgr_intg_err is used nowhere else in the top level.

design.text: The flash life cycle management interface encountered a program error.
design.note: FAULT_STATUS.prog_err (bit 3), which continues: "This could be a program integrity error, see !!STD_FAULT_STATUS for more details."

generated_from_same_input: D1, D5, D6, D8, D9 and D11 are in flash_ctrl.hjson.tpl, from which each top's register description, register RTL and registers.md are generated; those generated files are not counted as further evidence. D2, D3, D4, D7, D10 and D12 are in the hand-written RTL (flash_ctrl.sv.tpl is a template, written by hand). R1 to R4 are in the hand-written template document; each top's generated copy has the same lines.
finding: Each error is recorded where the documents say only in part. A program integrity error in an operation software started is recorded in ERR_CODE and in STD_FAULT_STATUS.PROG_INTG_ERR, as R1 and R2 say, but ERR_CODE's field is PROG_ERR, not PROG_INTG_ERR. In an operation the life cycle management interface started, it is recorded in FAULT_STATUS, as R4 says, but again as PROG_ERR; FAULT_STATUS has no integrity field. A read integrity error of that interface is recorded in a field named LCMGR_INTG_ERR, as R3 says, but in STD_FAULT_STATUS, not FAULT_STATUS. Software that reads the fields R1, R3 or R4 name finds no such field in that register.
missing_information: This case reads the register description and the RTL that sets the fields; it does not simulate an integrity error.
ambiguities: R1 and R4 could be read as naming the error rather than a field. At this revision the program controller sets prog_err only for a program integrity error (D2), so the fields they would then mean are ERR_CODE.PROG_ERR and FAULT_STATUS.PROG_ERR; the field names written still do not exist.
out_of_scope: The flash_ctrl of each top is generated from this template with top-specific parameters; the register fields compared here are the same in every top at this revision.
